questions.text: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
questions.explanation: The Rasoolullah (PBUH) was born in Makkah Mukarramah.

questions.text: In pre-Islamic Arabia, the Arabs' eloquence and memory found expression in:
questions.explanation: The Arabs had remarkable memory and eloquence, which found expression in poetry.

questions.text: At which place was a yearly fair held for poetical competitions?
questions.explanation: Every year a fair was held for poetical competitions at Ukaz.

questions.text: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) begin spending most of his time in solitude and meditation?
questions.explanation: When he was thirty-eight he spent most of his time in solitude and meditation.

questions.text: In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meditate?
questions.explanation: He used to retire to the cave of Hira with food and water to remember Allah.

questions.text: Which angel brought the first revelation?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Jibril came to him in the cave of Hira with Allah's message.

questions.text: The first revealed verses begin with the command:
options: Read in the name of thy Lord
questions.explanation: 'Read in the name of thy Lord Who created...' (Quran 96:1-5).

questions.text: For how many years did the revelation continue?
questions.explanation: The revelation continued for the next twenty-three years.

questions.text: The word 'solitude' means:
questions.explanation: Solitude is the state of being alone, especially when you find it pleasant.

questions.text: What does 'patriotism' mean?
options: Love for the motherland or devotion to one's country
questions.explanation: Patriotism means love for the motherland or devotion to one's country.

questions.text: The word 'patriot' comes from the Latin word:
questions.explanation: It comes from the Latin word 'patriota', which means countryman.

questions.text: According to the text, the supreme values for a patriot are:
options: sovereignty, integrity and honour of the country
questions.explanation: For a patriot, the sovereignty, integrity and honour of the country are supreme values.

questions.text: Who led the Muslims of the subcontinent in their struggle for a separate homeland?
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam secured a separate homeland for the Muslims.

questions.text: In which wars did many brave soldiers lay down their lives for Pakistan, according to the text?
questions.explanation: Many soldiers laid down their lives in the wars of 1965, 1971 and Kargil.

questions.text: 'Patriotism is a commendable quality' is a statement of:
questions.explanation: It expresses a judgement, so it is an opinion; facts can be proved with evidence.

questions.text: The cause is why something happens; the effect is:
questions.explanation: The cause is why something happens, and the effect is what happens as a result.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Daffodils'?
questions.explanation: 'Daffodils' is by William Wordsworth (1770-1850).

questions.text: In the first line, the poet compares himself to a:
questions.explanation: 'I wandered lonely as a cloud' — a simile comparing himself to a cloud.

questions.text: Where did the poet see the daffodils?
options: Beside the lake, beneath the trees
questions.explanation: 'Beside the lake, beneath the trees, fluttering and dancing in the breeze.'

questions.text: How many daffodils did the poet see at a glance?
questions.explanation: 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance, tossing their heads in sprightly dance.'

questions.text: The daffodils are compared to stars that shine on the:
questions.explanation: 'Continuous as the stars that shine and twinkle on the milky way.'

questions.text: What colour were the daffodils?
questions.explanation: 'A host of golden daffodils.'

questions.text: When do the daffodils flash upon the poet's 'inward eye'?
options: When he lies in vacant or pensive mood
questions.explanation: 'For oft, when on my couch I lie in vacant or in pensive mood, they flash upon that inward eye.'

questions.text: 'Fluttering and dancing in the breeze' gives the daffodils human qualities. This is called:
questions.explanation: Giving human actions like dancing to flowers is personification.

questions.text: The 'inward eye' in the poem refers to:
questions.explanation: The inward eye is the mind's memory, 'the bliss of solitude'.

questions.text: In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madinah?
questions.explanation: He migrated with Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique to Madinah in 622 A.D.

questions.text: Hazrat Asma (RA) was the daughter of:
questions.explanation: Hazrat Asma was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique.

questions.text: Which title did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) give Hazrat Asma (RA)?
questions.explanation: For tying the food with her own belt, she was given the title of (Zat-un-)Nitaqain.

questions.text: Why was Hazrat Asma (RA) given this title?
options: She tied the food on the camel with her own belt
questions.explanation: She tied the food on the camel's back with her own belt as nothing else could be found.

questions.text: In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr hide during the migration?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Asma secretly carried food every night to the cave of Thawr.

questions.text: Who slapped Hazrat Asma (RA) when she would not tell where her father was?
questions.explanation: Abu Jehl slapped her so hard that her ear-ring fell off, but she did not reveal the secret.

questions.text: What did Hazrat Asma (RA) reply when Abu Jehl asked 'Where is your father?'
questions.explanation: She wisely replied with a counter question, 'How would I know?'

questions.text: Hazrat Asma's grandfather, Hazrat Abu Quhafa, was:
questions.explanation: Her grandfather Hazrat Abu Quhafa was very old and blind.

questions.text: Which prominent businesswoman of Makkah is given as an early example of a woman entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Khadija was a prominent businesswoman known for wisdom, integrity and leadership.

questions.text: Entrepreneurship is the process of:
options: starting and running a business, taking financial risks for profit
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship means starting and running a business, taking on financial risks and seeking profit.

questions.text: What do Microfinance Institutions offer to women in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions offer loans to help women start small businesses.

questions.text: Which is a challenge for women entrepreneurs mentioned in the lesson?
questions.explanation: Traditional gender roles that prioritise household duties create barriers for women.

questions.text: What provides platforms for female entrepreneurs to network and showcase products?
questions.explanation: Women's chambers of commerce provide platforms to network and showcase products.

questions.text: The story of Hazrat Khadija shows that:
options: gender should not be a barrier to success
questions.explanation: She became a symbol of empowerment, showing gender should not be a barrier to success.

questions.text: What was Taseer's one flaw?
questions.explanation: Despite his good qualities, he was terribly weak in managing his time.

questions.text: How did Taseer waste his time?
questions.explanation: He spent hours on video games, chatting with friends and daydreaming.

questions.text: Who decided to teach Taseer a lesson about time?
questions.explanation: His grandfather, a wise old man, decided to impart a valuable lesson.

questions.text: What was in the basket the grandfather showed Taseer?
questions.explanation: There was an empty jar and a basket with big rocks, pebbles and sand.

questions.text: Why could Taseer not fit the big rocks into the jar?
options: He put the sand and pebbles in first
questions.explanation: He poured in sand and pebbles first, leaving no room for the big rocks.

questions.text: What did the grandfather put into the jar first?
questions.explanation: He placed the big rocks first, then pebbles, then sand filled the gaps.

questions.text: The big rocks in the jar stand for:
options: the most important tasks in life
questions.explanation: The lesson: put important tasks first; smaller things fit around them.

questions.text: 'Procrastinating' means:
options: delaying tasks that should be done
questions.explanation: Procrastination is putting off work, as Taseer did, until it piles up.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'If'?
questions.explanation: 'If' is by Rudyard Kipling (1865-1936).

questions.text: Which famous book was written by Rudyard Kipling?
questions.explanation: Kipling is best known for works such as The Jungle Book, Kim and The Man Who Would Be King.

questions.text: Where was Rudyard Kipling born?
questions.explanation: He was born in the British colonial subcontinent, which influenced much of his writing.

questions.text: According to the poem, Triumph and Disaster should be treated as:
questions.explanation: 'If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster and treat those two impostors just the same.'

questions.text: 'If you can keep your head when all about you are losing theirs' means:
questions.explanation: Keeping your head means staying calm and sensible when others panic.

questions.text: 'If you can dream — and not make dreams your ___'
questions.explanation: 'If you can dream — and not make dreams your master.'

questions.text: The main theme of 'If' is:
options: qualities of a balanced and mature person
questions.explanation: The poem lists qualities like patience, honesty and self-control that make a person mature.

questions.text: In 'neither... nor', 'not only... but also', the words are called:
questions.explanation: Pairs like neither/nor and not only/but also are correlative conjunctions.

questions.text: In 'He could not attend the meeting because he was sick', 'because' is a:
questions.explanation: 'Because' joins a dependent clause to an independent clause: a subordinating conjunction.

questions.text: Which products does Pakistan export, according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: We export textiles, rice and sports goods to countries all over the world.

questions.text: Which initiative is mentioned as bringing foreign direct investment to Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Foreign direct investment, especially through CPEC, brings capital and technology.

questions.text: What has accelerated globalisation?
options: Advances in technology, transportation and communication
questions.explanation: Advances in technology, transport and communication have accelerated globalisation.

questions.text: How has digital globalisation helped students?
options: They can learn about different cultures through websites and videos
questions.explanation: Students can learn about cultures, traditions and histories through websites, videos and articles.

questions.text: Social media interaction between cultures promotes:
questions.explanation: Seeing how others live and celebrate helps promote empathy.

questions.text: Jobs created by multinational companies in Pakistan often offer:
questions.explanation: These jobs often offer better pay and working conditions than local companies.

questions.text: According to the lesson, education fosters economic growth, reduces poverty and promotes:
questions.explanation: Education fosters growth, reduces poverty, promotes gender equality and helps protect the environment.

questions.text: Which subjects help students develop critical thinking and problem-solving?
questions.explanation: Mathematics, science and technology develop critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

questions.text: 'Human capital' refers to:
options: the knowledge, skills and health people accumulate
questions.explanation: Human capital is the knowledge, skills and health individuals accumulate over their lives.

questions.text: Quality education can reduce:
questions.explanation: By preparing students for industries, quality education reduces unemployment and underemployment.

questions.text: Quality education acts as a 'leveller', meaning it:
questions.explanation: It provides equal opportunities for all, regardless of socio-economic background.

questions.text: Which skills does quality education emphasise for employability?
options: Literacy, numeracy, digital literacy and vocational skills
questions.explanation: These skills enhance employability and economic independence.

questions.text: The snow leopard is often called the:
questions.explanation: The snow leopard is often referred to as the 'Ghost of the Mountains'.

questions.text: Up to what altitude does the snow leopard roam?
questions.explanation: It roams at altitudes as high as 5,500 metres.

questions.text: How do the snow leopard's long tails help it?
questions.explanation: Their long tails help them balance on narrow ledges.

questions.text: The markhor's horns are shaped like a:
questions.explanation: The markhor has impressive corkscrew-shaped horns.

questions.text: The name 'markhor' means ___ in Persian.
questions.explanation: 'Markhor' means 'snake-eater' in Persian, referring to horns like coiled snakes.

questions.text: What does the markhor eat?
questions.explanation: The markhor is a herbivore feeding on grasses, shrubs and leaves.

questions.text: The snow leopard and the markhor are a classic example of:
questions.explanation: Snow leopards rely on markhors for food — a classic predator-prey relationship.

questions.text: If the snow leopard disappeared, according to the lesson:
options: it would create a ripple effect harming the ecosystem
questions.explanation: As a top predator it keeps the balance; its loss would cause a ripple effect.

questions.text: Who wrote the one-act play 'The Dear Departed'?
questions.explanation: 'The Dear Departed' is by William Stanley Houghton (1881-1913).

questions.text: Who is Mr. Abel Merryweather in the play?
options: Father of Amelia Slater and Elizabeth Jordan
questions.explanation: Abel Merryweather is the father of Amelia Slater and Elizabeth Jordan, and grandfather of Victoria.

questions.text: Victoria Slater is the daughter of:
questions.explanation: Victoria is the daughter of Amelia and Henry Slater.

questions.text: Where is the whole play set?
options: In the living room of the Slater family's house
questions.explanation: The play's sole location is the living room of the Slaters' house.

questions.text: Which items do the Slaters secretly take from grandfather's room?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Slater and Henry carry down grandfather's bureau and take his clock.

questions.text: Mrs. Slater tells Victoria not to tell her aunt about the:
questions.explanation: 'Victoria, don't breathe a word to your aunt about the clock and the bureau.'

questions.text: A one-act play typically has:
options: a single act, focused plot and limited characters
questions.explanation: A one-act play unfolds in one act with a straightforward plot, few characters and one setting.

questions.text: The play 'The Dear Departed' mainly criticises:
questions.explanation: The daughters' rush to divide their father's belongings exposes greed and selfishness.
